messages:
DeployBot: rollout complete: release v3.2.1 -> prod (all regions). flip: inference-gateway, routing v3.2.1 100% :rocket:
PagerBot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: inference-gateway timeouts and 5xx spike — error-rate 18% in us-west-2, p95/p99 latency climb. Alert group: gateway-timeouts.
Dan: I'm oncall, taking. pulling up dashboards and traces now. tagging eng-sre.
Alex: noted, diving into connection pools and proxy timeouts. can someone post the deploy hash?
Maya: deploy hash: b7f9c3e. main change was async-kv-affinity + small routing refactor. canary metrics looked fine (2% traffic).
Priya: customer impact: SupportOps says a number of requests returning 504/502, some timed out in chat flows. CS is getting escalations from two customers about slow responses.
SupportOps: confirmed, three paid accounts reported request failures since ~00:08 UTC. opening bridge with account owners.
Dan: p95 went from ~120ms -> 850ms; p99 from 1.2s -> 6.4s. error-rate jumped from 1.6% -> 18% in us-west-2. request volume hasn't increased noticeably. looks like a regression post-deploy.
Alex: looking at gateway logs: increased queueing on grpc-proxy. many backpressure errors: `error: kv-cache wait timeout` and `rpc: connection reset by peer`.
Maya: kv-affinity change pinned traffic to fewer backends during warmup. we see slow KV lookups with higher tail latency at the model sharded layer. likely TTL/warmup interaction.
Priya: mitigation options: 1) immediate rollback to v3.2.0, 2) enable graceful-fallback-circuit to route to unsharded model variant, 3) reduce max-concurrency at gateway to shed load and avoid 5xx.
Dan: rolling back is fastest. if rollback takes too long, we can enable fallback-circuit. I'm preparing rollback command.
Alex: if we rollback, need to ensure KV cache warmup won't be hit again on re-deploy. also check autoscaler didn't scale down pods unexpectedly.
Dan: issuing rollback now: `kubectl -n inference rollout undo deployment/inference-gateway --to-revision=2`
DeployBot: rollback initiated for deployment/inference-gateway -> target revision 2. watch pods for ready state.
Maya: note: the deployed image had a change to the connection pool default from 512 -> 1024, combined with affinity change that caused a hotpath on a subset of nodes. fallback-circuit will route to non-affine pool path which is safer.
Alex: checking logs during rollback: pod replacement in progress; old pods terminating.
Dan: rolling back proved quick — new pods are becoming ready. health checks greening.
SupportOps: customers reporting partial recovery, some still seeing occasional 504s, but volume of errors dropping.
Priya: metrics update: error-rate down to 3.5% in us-west-2 within 3 minutes of rollback; p95 back to ~150ms, p99 ~1.4s.
Maya: leaving a temporary guard: enabling fallback-circuit and setting weight to 0.1 for v3.2.1 routes in case of drift. command: `redwood route set-weight --service=inference --from=v3.2.1 --to=v3.2.0 --weight=0.9`
Alex: adding short-term throttle: `gateway.set_concurrency(200)` to reduce queueing while caches warm.
Dan: doing a quick post-rollback checklist: confirm no pending deploys, validate canary config increased to 10% for future canaries, file an incident page.
SupportOps: continuing to triage customer tickets and sending status updates. recommend one more customer message saying mitigation is in place and engineers are investigating root cause.
Priya: planning: we should pin affinity feature behind feature-flag and add a KV warmup step in the rollout runbook. also add a health check for kv-tail-latency for canaries.
Maya: capture heap/profiler from the affected pod group and store traces under /artifacts/5371110000 for postmortem.
Alex: handing off to next oncall in 12m; Dan will create the incident page and assign SEV: s1. make sure postmortem owner is set.
Dan: creating incident doc now and will follow up with RCA. thanks all — keeping bridge open for 15 more minutes then transitioning to async updates. :thumbsup:
